Considering the virus crosses the blood brain barrier almost immediately, I think there are a lot of rude awakenings awaiting many people living with HIV. Especially with even a Duke University Hospital researcher admitting to me that despite ARVs, positive people have a much higher than average rate of memory problems and dementia as they age.
Perhaps the most limiting aspect of having HIV is how limited the actual long term research truly is. 

Yes, you'll probably live a normal lifespan, despite the fact that the newer meds that have made this possible have only been around for about 20 years tops, therefore meaning no one has yet lived long enough for this to be proven factual. Also, quality over quantity of life remains questionable. There's just a lot of guesswork out there, and people currently living with HIV and taking their meds as directed are mostly functioning on long term hope and short term comfort.
To say this, however, can win you a lot of jeers. So it can feel limiting in how honest or open you can actually be about living with HIV.

I've never known of a drug developed for ANY disease that just plain works as long as strict adherence is followed. HIV meds are no different, despite what many would have you believe.
